I will keep things simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, I would put all my land into the usual wheat and summer maize rotation, because that is what I know best, it fits the local weather and water conditions, and at my age I would rather choose a stable system than something risky or too labor-intensive. I will keep winter wheat on the land through early summer, then follow immediately with summer maize after harvest so the land does not sit idle. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want more even emergence, better disease tolerance, and more reliable yield. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, jointing-stage nutrition, three irrigations if water allows, and a couple of pesticide sprays mainly for weeds and disease. After wheat harvest, I will sow maize quickly, use no-tillage or very light disturbance to save labor and preserve moisture, apply nitrogen in split doses, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and keep pesticide use limited to what is necessary for weeds and insects. My goal is not the highest possible yield, but a dependable harvest with manageable work and cost.
